title: Vanguard sessions with Skeeter Best and Coleman Hawkins; Under the Sweetheart Tree
summary: Thompson describes his Vanguard trio and Hawkins sessions, a tune by his first wife June Evans, and the Parker tunes Street Beat, Tune Us In and 20th Century Blues.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: My first record date: sessions, personnel, discography

blocks.x: I'd like to hear about those Vanguard records.

Well, I made several Vanguard records, some of which were first with a trio, a trio of guitar, bass and drums. They were done with Skeeter Best, a very, very fine guitarist and Aaron Bell, who had played with Duke Ellington bass, and myself on piano. And we later incorporated some other musicians for later sessions, but it was fundamentally the trio session that I recorded first, you know. And I had on there some original songs, also, which I dedicated one of the numbers to my old friend Sonny Howard. I called it 'Sonny Howard's Blues.' And some other very original creations of mine.

Now, I also made some recordings with -- featuring Coleman Hawkins on Vanguard label, and on this particular session I had Earl Warren on alto saxophone, one of the old Count Basie men who was such a great first saxophone player, and along with Benny Morton on the trombone, who had also been with Count Basie and a great trombonist. And I had Joe Newman on trumpet, and I had -- let's see, O. C. Johnson on drums, and -- oh, I had -- I can't name all these musicians, but these were some of my most memorable recordings, along with
Coleman Hawkins being on my recordings. I had formerly played with him on his.
And he had come over and played some with mine. And one of the songs was an original piece that I had written featuring him.

It was called 'Under the Sweetheart Tree.' Actually it was written by my first wife, whose name was June Evans, and she played the piano, very beautiful classical piano, and she was interested in arranging and composing music. She was very highly inspired by Duke Ellington and Lionel Hampton, the combination of the two. And she was a very good classical pianist.

And I recorded this song that she wrote, and it was called 'Under the Sweetheart Tree,' featuring Coleman Hawkins on these Vanguard recordings. And it was these recordings with him, and the ones that I'd done with Charlie Parker earlier, which featured Charlie Parker as a member of my group, that to me were some of the highlights of my arranging and recording with my own group. You see what I mean?
Yes, I do. Can you think of any of the titles when you used Charlie Parker? Can you recall those titles?
Yeah, I told you awhile ago, 'Street
Beat, and some other. 'Tune Us In' and some others. Oh, yes, that's right.
